# Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack — facts

> Source-anchored units about Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack: 15 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Definitions

- [statement] RRF is a useful baseline, not a guarantee of optimal relevance: Bruch, Gai and Ingber found tuned convex score combination stronger in their tested in-domain and out-of-domain settings; Elastic also reports that calibrated weighted scoring can outperform RRF while requiring dataset-specific evaluation. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11934 · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack · also: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/improving-information-retrieval-elastic-stack-hybrid

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] In its vendor-run benchmark on six datasets, OpenSearch reports RRF averaging 3.86% lower NDCG@10 than its score-based hybrid pipeline, with average latency improvements of 1.62% at p50 and 0.78% at p99. These are within-OpenSearch fusion comparisons, not Atlas comparisons or measured TCO savings. (low confidence) — https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/ · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Evaluation inference: compare both architectures at matched relevance, freshness requirements and end-to-end latency, and include synchronization engineering alongside retrieval infrastructure. Native fusion alone cannot establish lower TCO because embedding/index work remains and fusion algorithms can change relevance and latency. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/harness-power-atlas-search-vector-search-with-rankfusion · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack · also: https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/, https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/strategic-database-architecture-for-ai-unified-vs-split

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Reciprocal rank fusion sums contributions based on document rank rather than averaging raw BM25 and vector similarity scores. This avoids having to normalize those incompatible raw score scales before merging. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/hybrid-search-ranking, https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/
- [statement] Built-in hybrid fusion is not exclusive to Atlas: Azure AI Search documents parallel text/vector retrieval followed by RRF, and OpenSearch provides an RRF search pipeline. A fair consolidation comparison must include these integrated alternatives rather than assuming every alternative needs separate lexical and vector engines. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/hybrid-search-ranking · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack · also: https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/
- [statement] MongoDB identifies duplicated identifiers or metadata, propagation of creates/updates/deletes, reconciliation, and additional document-fetch round trips as engineering costs of an operational database plus separate vector store. This is a vendor architectural argument; the article supplies no controlled Atlas-versus-split dollar saving for hybrid search. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/strategic-database-architecture-for-ai-unified-vs-split · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas $rankFusion combines full-text and vector retrieval pipelines in one aggregation query, removing the need to implement the ranked-list merge in application code. This consolidates orchestration; it does not eliminate the underlying retrieval operations. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack · also: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/harness-power-atlas-search-vector-search-with-rankfusion
- [statement] Atlas documents weighted RRF as the sum of w/(60+r) over pipelines containing a document. Pipeline weights are configurable, while Atlas fixes the rank constant at 60. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/hybrid-search-ranking
- [statement] The Atlas implementation example still creates separate text and vector indexes and computes document and query embeddings. Native fusion removes client merging code but does not remove those index and embedding responsibilities from capacity and cost planning. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/harness-power-atlas-search-vector-search-with-rankfusion · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack
- [statement] MongoDB documents serial execution of $rankFusion sub-pipelines, a same-collection requirement, and no pagination support. A single client request therefore does not imply parallel retrieval or suitability for every existing search application. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack
- [statement] Hybrid retrieval is also available within other search platforms: Azure AI Search documents parallel query execution followed by RRF; Elastic demonstrates native lexical/semantic fusion. A separate lexical engine plus separate vector database is therefore not the only alternative to Atlas. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/hybrid-search-ranking · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack · also: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/improving-information-retrieval-elastic-stack-hybrid
- [statement] For a TCO comparison, native fusion alone is insufficient evidence of a cost advantage. Inference from the implementation and fusion studies: compare equivalent judged relevance, candidate depths and latency, then price embeddings, indexes, compute and operational integration for each architecture. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/harness-power-atlas-search-vector-search-with-rankfusion · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack · also: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/improving-information-retrieval-elastic-stack-hybrid, https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11934
- [statement] The GitHub advisory for CVE-2026-8063 describes an authenticated crash from $rankFusion or $scoreFusion with an empty input pipeline on a view, affecting MongoDB Server 8.2 before 8.2.7. The advisory is marked unreviewed and links SERVER-121851; it is version-specific evidence, not proof that ordinary hybrid queries are unreliable. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v547-m6pg-pf7w · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack
- [statement] RRF scores are ranking outputs, not cosine similarities: their scale depends on the lists and weights being fused. Reusing a vector-similarity threshold for fused results is therefore an invalid comparison. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/hybrid-search-ranking
- [statement] MongoDB recommends limiting each fusion input pipeline and adjusting lexical/vector weights per query. Candidate depth and weighting remain workload-specific relevance and resource decisions after fusion is consolidated into the database. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs separate search plus vector stack
